summary: Elevated 5xx rate on long-polling/streaming routes during customer scraping window
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NotesNow reported a ~8-12% elevated 5xx rate (predominantly 502/503) on dedicated streaming/long-poll routes between 02:00-03:15 UTC. Errors coincide with a periodic scraping job the customer runs (long-held HTTP connections).

Impact:
- NotesNow experiences dropped streaming sessions and occasional fallback to retries; user-visible degradation for ~5k active sessions during window.
- Elevated error rate also increased host CPU/thread contention and caused short-lived upstream restarts.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant (NotesNow) on prod us-east-1 cluster; Dedicated pool: rdx-dedicated-08; ephemeral proxy version: 2.3.1; gateway: apigw-1.12.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer runs periodic scraper that opens long-poll HTTP streams (duration ~150s) at scale every 15m.
2) During the scrape window, keepalive / accept queue grows, and apigw backlog increases.
3) Ephemeral-proxy threads repeatedly wake and incur epoll churn; kernels fall back to slower poll paths and threadpool queues increase.
4) Short-lived upstream runtime restarts and 502/503 return to client.

Initial hypothesis:
- Long-lived connections plus high concurrency expose a memory retention path in ephemeral-proxy causing threadpool exhaustion under epoll wake storms.
- Backpressure from keepalive-heavy traffic propagates to the serving runtime, causing prefetch cancellations and connection resets.

Observations / logs (sanitized):
- apigw metrics (02:05 UTC): accept_queue_depth=1843, active_streams=5120, 5xx_rate=0.089
- proxy stderr:
  2026-03-14T02:06:12Z ERROR accept_queue: backlog=1821 wakeups=12421 threadpool_wait=0.87s
  2026-03-14T02:07:03Z WARN mem: rss=1.9GB heap_uncollected=430MB slow_gc_count=3
  2026-03-14T02:08:01Z ERROR upstream: connect_reset by peer (runtime reclaimed)
- runtime logs show repeated prefetch cancellation traces followed by SIGTERM from watchdog when worker queue > 5000

Telemetry links:
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/notesnow/streams/errors?from=2026-03-14T02:00Z&to=2026-03-14T03:30Z
- Traces: https://jaeger.redwood/trace/notesnow/abcd1234

Customer notes:
- The customer confirmed they ramped a new scraping job last week that increased simultaneous long-held streams by ~3x. They can temporarily reduce concurrency if requested.
investigation_notes:
- 02:30: captured pmap/heap snapshots from one affected ephemeral-proxy host: observed growing ephemeral thread-local caches not freed between requests.
- Heap profile suggests retained buffers from long-poll path (splice buffers) are not released until process restart; reproducer run (internal) opened 6k long connections and memory increased steadily.
- Correlation between keepalive interval and accept queue growth: shorter keepalive -> more frequent epoll wakeups and higher thread churn.
- We reproduced accept_queue growth in staging with a scripted client that holds connections for 120-180s; reproduced apigw backlog and increased 502 returns when threadpool saturation hit.
- No indication of GPU OOM or model-level crashes; upstream runtime restarts were graceful watchdog-driven due to threadpool overload.
root_cause: A memory retention/regression in ephemeral-proxy (long-poll code path) combined with high concurrent long-lived connections. The retention increases threadpool blocking and epoll wake churn which propagates backpressure to the serving runtime and causes transient upstream restarts and 5xx responses.
mitigation_actions:
- Short-term: support team applied a per-tenant connection cap for NotesNow during next scheduled scrape window (reduced concurrency from 6k -> 1500). This reduced accept_queue to <400 and 5xx_rate returned to baseline.
- Immediate tech mitigation: increased accept_queue tuning on apigw for dedicated pool and temporarily enabled keepalive coalescing on the proxy side.
- Hotfix: engineering built a GC/tuning patch and a fix for buffer release in ephemeral-proxy (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ephemeral-proxy/pull/8423). Deployed canary 2.3.4 to 10% of traffic at 2026-03-14T10:15Z.
resolution:
Partial: Canary rollout of ephemeral-proxy v2.3.4 shows no accept_queue growth under same repro load in staging. Customer concurrency cap remains in place until full rollout. Plan to promote the hotfix to 100% after 24h monitoring.

Workaround provided to customer:
- Reduce concurrent scraper clients (recommended multiplier x0.25)
- If immediate reduction not possible, schedule staggered scrapes offset by 30s windows to avoid synchronized spikes

Follow-up items:
- Engineering to promote v2.3.4 to production across dedicated pool (owner: Priya Nair).
- Add per-route long-poll circuit-breaker in apigw (owner: Runtime Platform).
- Instrumentation: add epoll wakeup metric and per-proxy retained-buffer gauge.
- Postmortem and runbook update (owner: SRE).
next_steps:
- Marcos monitoring canary metrics for 24h; report at 2026-03-15 10:30 UTC.
- Priya to open promotion PR for full rollout and coordinate maintenance window if necessary.
- CS to follow up with NotesNow contact Jason Lee to confirm scrape schedule changes and confirm visible improvement.
